calls.reconciliation: Five factual disputes. (1) Sep 16 FOMC: only Run 1 had post-decision reporting - 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00%, S&P +0.4% - consistent with Runs 2/3's 90-92.5% pre-pricing; accepted, but immaterial since both the Sep 16 and Oct 27-28 meetings fall outside Sep 21-Oct 2. (2) Hormuz framing: Run 1 treated the Sep 14 mine strike/blockade declaration as a fresh shock; Runs 2/3 document a crisis continuous since Feb 28 2026 with 72+ vessel incidents and a March Brent peak of $126. Runs 2/3 are far more specific and Run 1's own dossier notes gold FELL on Sep 14 despite the news - so this is a largely-priced chronic conflict, which cuts the pro-gold pull in the median while preserving an escalation tail. (3) Correlation: Run 3 alone flagged that gold and equities have been moving together on rate expectations; this is independently corroborated inside Runs 1 and 2's own dossiers (both report the Sep 14 joint decline). ρ ≈ 0.25 rather than 0 cuts spread SD from ~6.3pp to ~5.1pp - the one correction that changes the answer. (4) Base rate: Run 1's +0.6pp is from a 2024-25-bull-contaminated class it disowns in its own reasoning; the two long-horizon classes agree on ~0.0. (5) Instrument, roll and the Sep 2 CR are unanimous and settled. Unsettleable from the dossiers: the exact measurement convention (Sep 18 close vs Sep 21 open as the start point, a ~1 trading day difference) and the Sep 16 dot plot's contents - Run 3 asserts a hawkish Warsh dot plot that no other run retrieved, so I do not lean on it. Remaining dispute is pure judgment: the runs shade the median to +0.2/0.0/+0.2 on a mild recent gold edge. With Hormuz downgraded to priced-in and no window-internal Fed event, I see nothing that beats the reference class, so I take the median to 0.0 with a small positive EV from residual right skew - lower than two of three runs on the center, and narrower than Runs 1/2 on width because of the correlation correction.
